title: Norbert (6 June)
hookLine: a courtier knocked from his horse by lightning who founded the Premonstratensians

cards: Lightning, on a country road. Below it, a rider in fine clothes, on his way somewhere that matters to him. A bolt strikes the ground in front of the horse, the horse rears, and the rider is thrown into the mud.
He lies there, stunned, rain on his face, and, the story goes, he hears a voice. Yesterday's saint never moved. Today's saint gets moved, hard.

teach.b: Norbert was a nobleman and a cleric at court in the German lands, with a comfortable life and good connections. Tradition remembers him as worldly, holding church positions without much interest in what they were for.

teach.h: THE QUESTION: WHAT WILT THOU HAVE ME DO?
teach.b: Lying on the ground, in the story, he asked what Paul had asked: "Lord, what wilt thou have me to do?" The answer was a line from a psalm. In the Douay-Rheims: "Turn away from evil and do good."
No vision of angels, no long speech. A line he'd have known by heart, suddenly aimed at him. The scene has an echo.
Paintings show Paul thrown from a horse on the road to Damascus.

teach.h: PAUL'S HORSE IS NOT IN ACTS.
teach.b: But read Acts, and there's no horse. The Douay-Rheims says only: "And falling on the ground, he heard a voice." The horse comes from the painters.
Norbert's story has a real one. He didn't change overnight into someone else. He did penance, was ordained a priest, and started preaching, barefoot, tradition says, from town to town.

teach.h: A FALL, THEN A LONG ANSWER.
teach.b: Then, at a remote place in France called Prémontré, he gathered men to live as canons: priests who pray the hours together like monks but go out to serve parishes.

teach.h: TURN AWAY FROM EVIL AND DO GOOD.
teach.b: From that place comes his order's long name, the Premonstratensians, also called, more simply, the Norbertines.

Later, as an archbishop, he worked to reform the clergy, the very kind of comfortable churchman he had once been. In his story, conversion is not one bright moment, but a fall, a question, and a long life of answering it.

how: Saint Norbert is remembered on 6 June; the Norbertine (Premonstratensian) canons and their parishes and schools keep it as their founder's feast, often with Mass and the Liturgy of the Hours sung together.

games.q: you're Norbert, lying in the mud after the lightning. what do you ask?
o: why did this happen to me?
Lord, what wilt thou have me to do?
games.why: in the story he asks Paul's own question, and the answer is a psalm line: turn away from evil and do good.

practice: Bring to mind one person caught in something that's hurting them, a habit or a hardness; maybe it's you. Hold them without lecturing, and wish them a good turning, in their own time.
If you pray, ask quietly, as Norbert did, Lord, what wilt thou have me to do, and leave room for an answer.

wordCard.voice: Norbert. A courtier thrown to the ground in a storm, who turned, preached, and founded the Norbertines at Prémontré.

carryVoice: Your line: knocked from his horse. For Norbert, the storm was only the beginning. Day nine hundred ninety-eight, done.
